name: Europe hybrid attacks
value: France blames IRGC for store sabotage
summary: France blamed an IRGC cyber unit on 9 Nov for sabotaging fridges at ~700 stores; Baltic drone alerts on 10–11 Nov
state: On 9 Nov France attributed the October sabotage of refrigeration systems at about 700 grocery stores, which caused food losses and at least 15 fires, to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of Iran's Revolutionary Guards; Paris summoned Iran's ambassador and is seeking EU sanctions (The Record). Drones entering from Belarus triggered shelter alerts across the Baltic states on 10–11 Nov, and Finland briefly restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland (Reuters via Al-Monitor). No casualties or repeated multi-country shutdowns were found as of 14 Nov, so the Alert line is not crossed.
for_you: Businesses running connected building or refrigeration systems are exposed to this kind of attack; the NCSC publishes guidance on securing operational technology. Travellers near Europe's eastern borders may meet short airspace closures.
rubric_hit: Watch: sabotage of ~700 French stores attributed by France to an Iranian state unit (9 Nov); no casualties or repeated multi-country shutdowns

sources.title: The Record — France blames Iran for fridge cyberattacks

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
